verdict.rationale: GitHub Projects documents an iteration field for week-by-week planning with breaks, kanban board and roadmap views, custom fields, built-in workflows, and customizable insights charts. Together these support sprint planning and management. However, the docs say Projects does not enforce a specific methodology, and the evidence shows no sprint-specific capabilities beyond iterations. missing for 10: documented sprint metrics such as velocity, burndown, or story-point estimation, sprint rollover or carry-over handling, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineer, I can plan and manage sprints for agile software development

citations.quote: An iteration field to plan work week-by-week, including support for breaks.
You can view your project as a high-density table layout, as a kanban board, or a timeline-style roadmap.
You can apply filters to the default chart and also create your own charts.
Built-in workflows allow you to automatically set fields when items are added or changed
